questions.question: Vijay sells bananas at the rate of Rs. 13 per dozen and earns a profit of 30 percent. The cost price of the bananas increases by 10 percent. If the selling price remains the same, then what is his new profit percent?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

Since the initial profit is 30%, Selling Price (SP) = 130 units.

The new CP increases by 10%, so New CP = 110 units.

Since the SP remains the same (130 units), New Profit = 130 − 110 = 20 units.

New Profit % = (20 ÷ 110) × 100 = 18.18%.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of bananas = Rs. 13 per dozen

Initial Profit = 30%

Cost Price increases by 10% and SP remains the same.

**Formula Used:**

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91479e78d83e8245bc1f567ee460f7c4a22ad02a82c1e5c77aaa1f0aee9d7f00.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial CP = (13 × 100) ÷ (100 + 30)

⇒ Initial CP = 1300 ÷ 130 = Rs. 10

⇒ New CP = Initial CP + 10% of Initial CP

⇒ New CP = 10 + (10 ÷ 100) × 10 = Rs. 11

⇒ The Selling Price remains the same, so New SP = Rs. 13

⇒ New Profit = New SP − New CP = 13 − 11 = Rs. 2

⇒ New Profit % = (New Profit ÷ New CP) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = (2 ÷ 11) × 100 = 18.18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount. Furthermore, Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given on an article, Effective Single Discount = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Trick

If a dealer sells goods at CP but uses a false weight, his Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

Volume of cone = (1/3) × (22/7) × r² × h

Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 14 × 14 × 12

Volume = 22 × 2 × 14 × 4 = 2464 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 2464 cm³.**

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × 22 × 2 × 14 × 12

⇒ Volume = 22 × 2 × 14 × (12 ÷ 3)

⇒ Volume = 22 × 2 × 14 × 4

The distance from the apex to any point on the circular base edge, given by l = √(r² + h²).

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

questions.question: A dealer marks his goods at 44% above the cost price. Then he allows 50% discount on it. What would be his loss percentage?

Mark-up rate = 44%

Discount = 50%

M.P = (100 + m)/100 × C.P

where, m = mark-up rate, M.P = marked price and C.P = cost price

S.P = (100 - d)/100 × M.P

where, d = discount, M.P = marked price and S.P = selling price

Loss% = (C.P - S.P)/C.P × 100

Let the C.P. be 100.

M.P = 144/100 × 100

M.P = 144

Now, the S.P will be:

S.P = (100 - 50)/100 × 144

S.P = 50/100 × 144

S.P = 72

Loss% = (100 - 72)/100 × 100

**Loss% = 28**

questions.question: There are 1200 men in a group. They have food for 80 days. After 5 days, 400 men left the group. Remaining food will last for how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining food is sufficient for **1200 men** for (80 − 5) = **75 days**.

Ratio of **Men** = 1200 : 800 = **3 : 2**.

Since **Men** and **Days** are inversely proportional, **Days ratio** = **2 : 3**.

2 units = 75 days ⇒ 1 unit = 37.5 days.

3 units = 37.5 × 3 = 112.5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 112.5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of men (M₁) = **1200**

Total provision duration = **80 days**

Number of days passed = **5 days**

Number of men who left = **400**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/463cb04cf0bb9ab0915c8cfc13c8a93774d1722dc58528fbf5ec2d799bc36536.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total Work (Provision) = **Men × Days**

M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂ (for remaining work)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Remaining days for the original group = 80 − 5 = **75 days**

⇒ Remaining men (M₂) = 1200 − 400 = **800 men**

⇒ Total remaining food in man-days = 1200 × 75

⇒ 1200 × 75 = 800 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = (1200 × 75) ÷ 800

⇒ D₂ = (12 × 75) ÷ 8

⇒ D₂ = (3 × 75) ÷ 2

⇒ D₂ = 225 ÷ 2

⇒ D₂ = **112.5 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 112.5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Formula)

The general relation is (M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Inverse Proportion

In food provision problems, the number of men is **inversely proportional** to the number of days the food lasts (M ∝ 1/D).

Effective Man-Days

Total provision can be measured in **man-days**. If men leave or join, calculate the remaining man-days and divide by the new strength.</p

questions.question: _______ unemployment refers to the lowest unemployment level a healthy economy can sustain without causing inflation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Natural unemployment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Natural unemployment:-**

 
 
• It is also known as the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment (NAIRU).
 
• It is the level of unemployment below which inflation starts to rise due to increasing labor costs.
 
• The natural rate of unemployment is determined by structural factors such as changes in technology, demographics, and globalization, and is beyond the control of monetary policy.
 
• The natural rate of unemployment can vary over time and across countries due to differences in labor market institutions, regulations, and social norms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Structural unemployment:-**

 
 
• It refers to the mismatch between the skills and qualifications of workers and the requirements of available jobs. 
 
• It can occur due to changes in the economy, such as technological advancements or shifts in consumer preferences.
 
 
 
• **Disguised unemployment:-**
 
 
• It refers to a situation where workers are employed but their contribution to production is negligible or redundant.
 
• It can occur in sectors with low productivity or in economies with a large informal sector.
 
 
 
• **Frictional unemployment:-**
 
 
• It refers to the temporary unemployment that occurs when workers are searching for better job opportunities or transitioning between jobs. 
 
• It can be reduced by improving labor market information and reducing search costs for job seekers.
